races.name: Radnor Hills Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Patagonia Girl
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer for Hugo Palmer who won over 12f on Good just 23 days ago; her sim-going record of 11/14 and her recent winning form (1st, then 2nd) suggests she's in a purple patch, and the 1m4½f trip at Chester suits a horse who stays strongly — David Probert will need a clean run off the final bend.
runners_data.comment: Patagonia Girl has distance and going experience to call on and a speed rating that edges ahead of her official mark, making her a genuine threat here; the worry is her recent finishing positions have been modest, with just one win in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Charmaine
runners_data.note: The only genuine prominent racer aside from Timber Twelve, making her positional role unusually valuable in a field full of closers; James Fanshawe's 34-day absence is not a concern given the stable's strike rate, but her limited Good-going form (3/15, no wins) in similar conditions is worth noting — she needs the pace to be fair, not slow.
runners_data.comment: Charmaine has been knocking on the door with a string of fourths in recent starts, and a runner-up finish four starts back shows she can go close — our rating of 88 makes her a leading threat off 141 lb, though she remains winless and needs to finally convert.

runners_data.name: Kuredu King
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason takes the ride on this Donald McCain stayer who has run well over today's trip before (3rd, 1st over 14f); the Good going appears fine for him, but his sim-going record of 8/12 with only one win and two places suggests consistency without dominance — the blinkered headgear is absent today and he'll need traffic to part off the home turn.
runners_data.comment: Ran third last time out after a 43-day break, and he has winning form in recent starts — a winner three starts back and again five starts back — but he carries 139 lb and our rating of 80 ranks him fifth of seven, suggesting he faces a stiff task here.

runners_data.name: Westerton
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish's six-year-old has a genuine hold-up profile, though the field's density of closers means he's shown in a more forward map position than he'll likely occupy; his recent form string (35059-) with a dash on the last run is a concern, and his longest win was over 22f — the 1m4½f trip here may be too short to fully express his staying strength.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Westerton nonetheless catches the eye on ratings — our figure of 90 has him top-rated, and he returns fit on 13 days' rest having run over today's trip and going before; the risk is that his recent form figures simply don't back it up.

runners_data.name: Timber Twelve
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's three-year-old is the only confirmed front-runner in the race and holds an enormous tactical advantage on this tight Chester track at a manageable weight of 135lbs; his Good-going form shows three wins from five runs and Ross Coakley can dictate every yard — the step up to 1m4½f from his last two runs over shorter is the key stamina question.
runners_data.comment: Timber Twelve catches the eye on recent form, winning one of his last two starts and boasting three wins in his last five; he has experience of today's trip and going, and 32 days between runs shouldn't inconvenience him. A trainer in lean form is the one note of caution.

runners_data.name: L'Eagle Aid
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's five-year-old is a hold-up type by nature, though the crowded closer's end of this field has pushed him into a midfield mapping that flatters his anticipated berth; his form string of 566353 and a sim-going record of 12/15 with two wins/six places suggests he finds ways into the frame — the hood (headgear: p) helps concentration, but Jack Callan's 3lb claim may not compensate for an awkward Chester draw.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, L'Eagle Aid has experience of today's trip and conditions but ranks sixth of seven on our figures — hard to fancy despite a third last time out and a third three starts back offering marginal encouragement.

runners_data.name: Level Look
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's lightly raced three-year-old is the least exposed runner in the field, with only four career runs, and Oisin Murphy's booking is a significant positive; naturally a hold-up horse who won over 10f on Standard, today's step to 1m4½f on Good at Chester is an open question — his sim-going record of just 1/4 with no wins or places on Good is a flag, and his redistributed position tempers confidence in a strong finish.
runners_data.comment: Level Look won two starts back but has finished fourth or worse in three of his last four, and our rating leaves him well below the field on these terms — hard to fancy despite the distance experience and a sharp enough turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Timber Twelve is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in a seven-runner field over 1m4½f at Chester, Ross Coakley should be able to dictate an entirely uncontested, controllable gallop from the front. Chester's tight, flat circuit amplifies the advantage of a horse that can control tempo — a lone leader here can effectively set the race up for itself, rationing the pace before quickening on the home turn. The redistributed trio of Westerton, Level Look, and L'Eagle Aid are all natural hold-up types nudged forward on the map simply because the field is saturated with closers; they are unlikely to genuinely challenge for early position, meaning the pace will remain singular and sustainable. This race shape decisively favours a hold-up horse with a strong turn-of-foot that can pounce on a leader who has controlled a modest gallop, or alternatively — and equally — the front-runner itself, who faces no pressure and may never be headed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Timber Twelve Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Timber Twelve bowls along at a measured pace with no rival willing to test him early, turning Chester's track into a gallop he dictates entirely.
scenarios.body: Coakley gets a soft lead through the first mile and rations the gallop, meaning the favourite can quicken rounding the home turn before rivals can mount a serious challenge; a horse with Timber Twelve's record of winning from the front on Good ground (3 wins) is tailor-made for this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Type Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just honest enough to set up a strong finish for a closer who has tracked without covering extra ground.
scenarios.body: A genuine hold-up horse with a clean passage around Chester's short home straight gets a clear run and overhauled a tiring Timber Twelve close home; Patagonia Girl's winning run over 12f on Good and Kuredu King's stamina profile make them the logical candidates.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Charmaine tracks the leader from second position and benefits from the even pace by outkicking the field in the straight.
scenarios.body: Charmaine, the one genuine prominent type in the field, follows Timber Twelve closely throughout and uses her track consistency over 12f on Good/Standard to collar him late; Fanshawe's patient approach and Muscutt's positional awareness on a tight track make this a credible secondary shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Timber Twelve sets too slow a pace, the field bunches and a late burst from a hold-up type results in a blanket finish.
scenarios.body: This shape depends on the redistributed hold-up horses — Westerton, Level Look, L'Eagle Aid — racing in a position that does not suit their natural style, making it the least structurally reliable scenario; Level Look, the youngest and least exposed runner, represents the marginal upside here if Oisin Murphy gets him into the race from an unusual position.

watchPoints.text: Timber Twelve — if Coakley is allowed to dictate a solo, uncontested lead at Chester, this horse becomes extremely difficult to reel in even for classier rivals, given the track's tight turns and short straight.

Patagonia Girl — Probert must secure a clean run around the home bend; Chester's narrow straight leaves hold-up horses vulnerable to traffic, and with three redistributed closers also seeking space, congestion late is a real risk.

Level Look — Oisin Murphy's presence elevates this horse on paper, but the Good-going sim record (1/4, no wins or places) and the trip extension to 1m4½f for a three-year-old with only four career runs introduces meaningful unknowns that Murphy alone cannot bridge.

Kuredu King — blinkered headgear is not listed today; monitor whether any equipment change has been made, as prior form may partly reflect headgear assistance, and a change could affect his early position and finishing effort.

Charmaine — her role as the only genuine second-slot prominent type is tactically significant; if she tracks Timber Twelve closely through the early stages, she becomes the most dangerous split-scenario horse regardless of her modest Good-going win record.

races.name: British Stallion Studs Ebf "confined" Maiden Stakes (For Horses Which Have Not Run More Than Three Times) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Pure Grit
runners_data.note: Placed twice on Good ground over 6f, fitting the track and conditions perfectly; Oisin Murphy is a major booking for Andrew Balding and adds tactical sharpness, though 64 days off the track is a slight concern despite the horse's consistency.

runners_data.name: Shakwaa
runners_data.note: Chester's lone front-runner with a recent run 31 days ago and a clean bill of health on Good 6f; Ed Walker's yard is firing at 9/38 (T14) and Kieran Shoemark knows how to construct a solo lead, making this horse the pivotal shape-setter for the entire race.

runners_data.name: Sovereigns High
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with only two runs, one on Good and one on Standard, so the form is thin and the ceiling genuinely unknown; Edward Greatrex rides and Ralph Beckett could have this horse primed for improvement, though the uncertain style (marked Unknown) means no confident positional read is possible.

runners_data.name: Therewearethen
runners_data.note: Has finished 9th and 10th on her two starts, both on Standard ground, and carries a confirmed tendency to fade in the closing stages — hold-up racing on Chester's flat 6f against a solo front-runner is a tough ask; Jennie Candlish's yard is modest at 5/22 (T14) and this profile looks the weakest in the field.

runners_data.name: Independent Roze
runners_data.note: Finished fifth on Good ground at 6f, which aligns well with today's conditions; Lisa Williamson's operation has returned 0 wins from 3 runners in the last 14 days and the claim of Faye McManoman is noteworthy, though hold-up tactics on a track that rarely rewards late finishers keep the ceiling modest.

races.paceDynamic: Shakwaa is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner maiden and, with no rivals likely to dispute the lead, she will dictate an uncontested, measured pace from the Chester starting gates. Pure Grit will slot in just behind from a prominent position, while Independent Roze and Therewearethen will track from the rear, though Therewearethen carries a known tendency to fade in the closing stages. With just five runners on a flat 6f Chester circuit and a lone leader setting a sustainable rhythm, there is no pace pressure to compress the field or generate a tactical scramble late. This race shape strongly favours the prominent-to-lead profile — horses racing on or near the pace from the outset will be best placed to control their own race, while genuine hold-up horses will have limited ground to make up on a front-runner who has been allowed to coast.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Shakwaa leads, holds on
scenarios.trigger: If Shakwaa bowls along uncontested and the pace remains measured throughout the 6f.
scenarios.body: Shakwaa dictates from flag to finish without a rival matching her early stride, conserving enough energy to quicken clear in the final furlong on Good ground she handles; with OR=120 and a recent run 31 days ago keeping her sharp, she is well-equipped to exploit a solo lead. Prominent Pure Grit is best placed to give chase, but Shakwaa's unchallenged gallop leaves chasers with too much ground to close.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent racer strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Shakwaa ties herself up setting a modest pace and Pure Grit pounces late from close quarters.
scenarios.body: Pure Grit has placed twice on Good ground at 6f and Andrew Balding's operation is in reasonable nick (T14: 8/45), meaning this well-placed pursuer could wear Shakwaa down if the pace is insufficient to build a winning buffer. Oisin Murphy's positioning and experience at the highest level gives Pure Grit every chance of seizing the initiative inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late and Independent Roze finishes strongly from off the speed.
scenarios.body: Independent Roze showed a solid fifth from a small sample on Good ground and, at a lighter 128lbs, carries the least weight; if the front two tie each other up in the closing stages, a late run from the rear could capitalise. However, Chester's flat 6f offers limited run-in for hold-up horses, and this scenario relies on a more compressed finish than the solo-pace dynamics suggest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race falls apart
scenarios.trigger: If Shakwaa misses the break or is withdrawn and Therewearethen or Sovereigns High steal it from a muddled start.
scenarios.body: Without Shakwaa controlling the pace, Sovereigns High — lightly raced and unexposed — could find a prominent position and take advantage of confusion in the early stages. Therewearethen's fading tendencies make her an unlikely winner, but Sovereigns High's unknown ceiling and Ralph Beckett's patient approach with young stock leave a sliver of hope in a chaotic scenario.

watchPoints.text: Shakwaa (front-runner) — if she misses the break at Chester's tight early bend, she may never recover her natural lead position and the entire pace map collapses.
Pure Grit — 64 days off the track means race-fitness is a live question; watch the paddock and early strides to confirm she is moving freely before treating her as a banker in tracking scenarios.

Therewearethen — the confirmed fading tendency in the finish is a significant red flag on a 6f flat track where there is nowhere to hide; monitor her odds movement for any signs of stable confidence contradicting the form.

Sovereigns High — lightly raced with only two runs and an unknown style tag; any market support before the off could indicate Ralph Beckett holds the horse in higher regard than the bare form suggests.

races.name: Queensferry Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Song Of The Clyde
runners_data.note: Clive Cox three-year-old who has shown real consistency at 6f on good ground, including a win, and Kieran Shoemark's booking adds confidence; naturally prominent and likely to secure a clean position just off Fitzella, which suits this race shape well.
runners_data.comment: Song Of The Clyde won three starts back and returns fit on 15 days' rest, with experience of both today's trip and going working in his favour at 130 lb from stall 8. The risk is that back-to-back seventh-place finishes since that win must be overcome.

runners_data.name: Ardisia
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's filly drops in OR from recent 7f efforts and reverts to 6f, where she has placed; 43 days between runs may mean she is fresh and ready to improve, and Cieren Fallon can place her prominently, though her 7f form raises mild stamina-in-reverse questions.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Ardisia nonetheless showed a glimpse of ability when third two runs back, and he has experience of both today's trip and going; 43 days off and 127 lb from stall four are the key questions as he seeks a return to that form.

runners_data.name: Calico Blue
runners_data.note: Consistent form string showing two wins and multiple placings at 5-6f on good ground, and Roger Varian's 10 winners in the past 28 days underlines stable confidence; however, this is a natural prominent racer whose position has been redistributed into midfield due to congestion, meaning she may not get the close-up berth her form demands.
runners_data.comment: Calico Blue arrives on the back of a win last time out, with two victories in his last five starts and a trainer firing at 36% in the past fortnight — he's a serious threat here. The main risk is whether his speed rating of 92 matches the level required.

runners_data.name: Jazl
runners_data.note: Three wins from six recent 6f starts on good ground make this a course-and-distance specialist for the Crisfords, and Jack Mitchell rides a strong book; nonetheless, Jazl is a front-running type pushed into a midfield role by the sheer number of prominent horses ahead of him, and his chance is meaningfully compromised if he cannot push through into the prominent group early.
runners_data.comment: Jazl won last time out and has run over today's trip, but he ranks bottom of the field on our figures and that unplaced effort two starts back sits awkwardly amid the wins; hard to fancy at these weights against stronger-rated rivals.

runners_data.name: Lifeplan
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in two career starts, both at 6f on good ground for Declan Carroll, which gives him a perfect profile for today's conditions; the concern is a 345-day absence, which is a major unknown for a lightly raced three-year-old, and Zak Wheatley's booking does not scream confidence despite the compelling form.
runners_data.comment: Lifeplan arrives on the back of back-to-back wins but has been off the track for 345 days, and our rating of 100 leaves him well below the top end of this field. The form he carries is encouraging, but fitness after such a lengthy absence is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Rock On Thunder
runners_data.note: The only genuine hold-up horse in the field; his best form comes over 6f on good ground (two seconds) and Kevin Stott is an astute judge of pace, but he needs the prominent bunch ahead to get competitive early if he is to arrive with a meaningful late run on this turning Chester track.
runners_data.comment: Twice runner-up in recent starts, Rock On Thunder has run over today's trip and going and rates a clear danger on our figures — but a trainer operating at just 4% over the past fortnight is the concern heading into this.

runners_data.name: Sirius A
runners_data.note: George Wood rides for James Horton's small but active string; this horse has a single course-appropriate win at 6f and is capable of sitting close to the pace, but his recent run of a fifth and a 23rd suggest inconsistency, and the step back from those marks needs explaining.
runners_data.comment: Shaped well enough in recent starts — a winner three starts back, placed second and third before that, but unplaced last time out after 44 days off gives pause; has run over today's trip and going, and 127 lb from stall one is the assignment.

runners_data.name: Fitzella
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner in the field, which gives David Probert a simple tactical blueprint from stall; her form figures on good ground are uninspiring (mostly fifth to eleventh), and while she will control the early fractions unchallenged, her repeated failure to win or place at this level raises the question of whether she can sustain the effort through the final furlong once rivals arrive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Fitzella nonetheless shows a solid profile here — she has run over today's trip and going before, is fit from a 23-day break, and our figures rate her 108, giving her a clear edge over most rivals from stall five at 122 lb.

runners_data.name: Simplify
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride on an Andrew Balding three-year-old who has won four of her last five starts, largely at 5f; she steps up to 6f today and, though capable at that trip, is a naturally prominent horse redirected into a midfield mapping by the crowded pace picture — if she cannot push forward to her comfort zone, her potent finishing speed may arrive too late on a track that rewards early positioning.
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Simplify makes it hard to build a case despite three wins in her last five starts — that unplaced run last time out is the flag, and 44 days off adds uncertainty, though she has distance and going experience and draws stall two.

races.paceDynamic: Fitzella is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to challenge her for the lead, she should establish a comfortable, metronomic gallop from the Chester start on her own terms. Behind her, however, lies a congested prominent group: Song Of The Clyde, Ardisia, Lifespan, and Sirius A all want to sit close to the pace, creating a queue for position that will generate sustained pressure from halfway and sharpen the sectionals through the final two furlongs. The field holds more prominent-types than can all secure their desired berth — Jazl, Calico Blue, and Simplify are true up-with-the-pace horses who are likely to find themselves shuffled into a midfield role through no choice of their own, meaning their chances are compromised by this race shape. With Fitzella controlling fractions and a solid pace chain behind her, this race strongly favours horses who can travel prominently, are comfortable on a true surface, and possess the finishing speed to pounce when the front-runner ties up in the final furlong — making the prominent-to-winner profile the dominant winning template here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fitzella leads, Prominent strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Fitzella dictates a fair but not suicidal pace and a genuine prominent horse travels fluidly to challenge inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Fitzella sets the tempo unchallenged, and one of the naturally prominent horses — able to sit just off her — finds the clearest run approaching the final furlong to overhaul her as she flattens out; this suits horses who can travel in the slipstream and kick on good ground without being baulked.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Fitzella steals an inch at the start, dictates a truly moderate gallop, and the prominent pack behind is too congested to mount a clean challenge.
scenarios.body: With a tactical, unchallenged pace and rivals getting in each other's way from 2f out, Fitzella simply keeps tabs on the energy expenditure and her rivals run out of ground; this shape rewards the solo pace-setter who avoids traffic and sustains a flat-out effort to the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closer Gets In
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scramble burns an abnormally fierce early pace and Fitzella is swallowed up, leaving a gap for a hold-up horse to come from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Rock On Thunder, the only genuine hold-up horse in the field, would be handed an unusually clean passage through beaten rivals; the scenario is narrow but real if the pace bunching creates genuine carnage 2f-3f out and the leader ties up sharply.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Collide
scenarios.trigger: If Jazl, Calico Blue, or Simplify manage to force their way into prominent ground early and the race turns into a sprint finish among crowded mid-pack horses.
scenarios.body: Racing out of their natural style and jostling for space, these redistributed prominent types would need a very specific set of circumstances — clean passage and the prominent queue ahead burning each other out — to benefit; their STYLE_FIT discounts make this the least likely winning shape.

watchPoints.text: Congestion alert 2f-3f out — with Song Of The Clyde, Ardisia, Lifeplan, and Sirius A all wanting to sit second or third, a tight bunch is likely to form behind Fitzella on the home turn, creating a genuine traffic flashpoint that could pocket runners on the rail.

Lifeplan's 345-day absence is the biggest unknown in the race — an unbeaten profile is enticing, but Carroll's lightly raced three-year-old has never been asked to perform at Listed level or after nearly a year off, and punters should wait to see how she warms up.

Jazl and Simplify will reveal their actual race position within the first furlong — if they can force their way forward from their wider draws they become significantly more dangerous; if they settle midfield as the map implies, their chances are structurally undermined.

Fitzella's front-running role should not be overstated — her best going figures show zero wins from 10 good-ground starts, and if a prominent horse travels smoothly in her wake, the leader's finishing kick is unproven at Listed level.

Rock On Thunder's headgear (previously worn) and a 44-day break are worth monitoring in the paddock — Kevin Ryan's runner needs a strongly run race to deliver late, and in a field where Fitzella controls the fractions, that strong pace cannot be guaranteed.

races.name: Disney's High School Musical At Lowry Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Palmar Bay
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's hold-up performer has run five times at 7f on Good going and found the winner on only one occasion; the short Chester straight and a tight circuit demand a perfect run from the back, but Harry Vigors's 5lb claim mitigates the 142lb weight and his 4/9 recent record at Chester distances is the most relevant stat here.
runners_data.comment: Palmar Bay arrives here in good order just 22 days since his last start, with experience of today's trip and going working in his favour, and our rating has him narrowly top of these rivals — the concern is he's winless in his last five starts, with that eighth last time out hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: The Strikin Viking
runners_data.note: Hamad Al Jehani's hold-up type drops back to 7f after a sequence run entirely over 6f, and while he won over 6f on Soft the trainer's 1/14 over 14 days is cold; the headgear flag and 0W3P on similar going underline that this horse needs a faster pace than Power Fizz is likely to supply.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win five starts back and has experience of today's distance and going, The Strikin Viking arrives here fresh enough on 26 days' rest. He has disappointed in recent starts but, drawn four carrying 142 lb, he is our pick to bounce back.

runners_data.name: Roman Dragon
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's seven-year-old carries a firm "fades in finish" flag that is particularly damning at Chester where the straight gives little room to recover; 14 runs on similar going with 2W3P sounds respectable but his last three finishes of 9th, 24th, and 11th tell a starker story and the hold-up style is poorly suited here.
runners_data.comment: Roman Dragon won five starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, returning after 22 days in solid order; the chief concern is that he has struggled for consistency in recent starts, with four runs since that victory failing to make the frame.

runners_data.name: Power Fizz
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner in the field, William Haggas and Cieren Fallon combine at 8/44 over 14 days which is solid strike-rate form; two wins at 7f on Good turf underpin the trip and going credentials, and an uncontested lead on a flat Chester circuit is the precise scenario this horse was built for — the 36-day absence is the only minor query.
runners_data.comment: Power Fizz won two starts back and has experience of today's trip and going, making him a serious threat off a 36-day break; the concern is an unplaced effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Dance In The Storm
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's prominent type slots neatly into the pace scenario from stall position, and Oisin Murphy's tactical intelligence makes him the most dangerous of those pressing Power Fizz; two wins at 7f on Good ground and a 45-day freshener for a yard running at 8/45 over 14 days is an encouraging profile, though the recent 17th and 10th finishes need explaining.
runners_data.comment: Ran well to win three starts back but has finished only fifth and then unplaced since, leaving her form hard to trust; has run over today's trip and going before, and a 45-day break could freshen her up, though she'll need to rediscover that earlier sparkle from stall ten.

runners_data.name: Khafiz
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's horse is a genuine hold-up type whose natural position at the rear of the field is unavailable in this race shape — he has been mapped to midfield, racing out of role; a 1W1P record on similar going over 7f at Chester trips is not without merit, and Kevin Stott offers competent handling, but the style mismatch structurally limits the ceiling.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Khafiz does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and his fourth last time out shows some residual form — but carrying 134 lb from stall 3, he'll need to find more than his recent efforts suggest.

runners_data.name: The Angel King
runners_data.note: Ian Williams's horse won over 7f on Soft but has shown 0W0P on the Good ground he faces today, and 58 days off the track is the longest lay-off in the field; his natural closing style cannot be expressed on this track in this race shape — he is squeezed into midfield by the weight of hold-up types, and the blank similar-going record is a red flag regardless.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, The Angel King is hard to fancy at this level; he does carry experience of today's trip and conditions, and stall two could be noted, but his recent form offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Korker
runners_data.note: K. R. Burke's seven-year-old has competed 15 times on similar going without a win and only three placed efforts; Jack Nicholls's 3lb claim helps with the 131lb burden, but 0W3P on comparable ground over 7-8f and a true closing style that cannot be delivered from a midfield slot in this pace map combine to make this a tough assignment.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Korker does bring distance and going experience to this, and a trainer firing at 26% in the past fortnight is a clear plus — though carrying 131 lb from stall nine on a 36-day break gives him plenty to overcome.

runners_data.name: Monarch's Gold
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy's lightly weighted three-year-old (128lb) is only 17 days from his last run and has two placed efforts on Good ground over 8f; dropping to 7f suits a prominent racer who can press Power Fizz, and Toby Moore's 7lb claim makes the weight comparison more flattering — the 0W2P on similar going is a caveat but the profile fits the likely race shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Monarch's Gold faces a stiff ask here; he does arrive on the back of a third last time out, has experience over today's trip and going, and 17 days between runs suggests he's fresh enough.

runners_data.name: Miami Matrix
runners_data.note: Patrick Morris has 0/10 over 14 days and Patrick Bradley takes a prominent ride on a horse that has finished 4th and 2nd at 7-8f on Good ground; the 83 OR is the lowest in the field and the trainer's cold recent form makes an upset difficult to construct, though the prominent style is at least compatible with the likely pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a ninth two runs back doing little to inspire confidence, Miami Matrix heads into this as the lowest-ranked runner on our figures; he has run over today's trip and going, and 22 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh enough.

races.paceDynamic: Power Fizz is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to push him from the outside, Cieren Fallon should be able to control tempo from the front on a flat, fair track at Chester. That uncontested lead sets up a sustainable, honest gallop rather than a breakneck pace — conditions that historically suit the horse that controls the race on this tight, turning circuit. Dance In The Storm and Monarch's Gold will press forward in prominent positions, keeping the pace honest without triggering a true war of attrition. The field contains more hold-up types than the track can accommodate in their natural slot: Khafiz, The Angel King, and Korker are all genuine closers mapped to midfield, meaning at least some will be racing out of their preferred role; of the three, Khafiz (Roger Fell, Kevin Stott) is most likely to secure the best of those forced positions. The race shape overwhelmingly favours horses who can either control from the front or travel prominently without cover — closers depending on a truly contested pace to generate a winning gap face a structural disadvantage today.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Power Fizz Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Power Fizz leads uncontested and dictates a fair, metronomic gallop from the front.
scenarios.body: Cieren Fallon slots Power Fizz across to the rail immediately, setting a pace that bleeds rivals' finishing kicks before the short Chester straight arrives; horses who press close on his quarters get first run. William Haggas's horse has won twice over this exact trip on Good turf and the solo lead role on a flat course plays directly to his strengths.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Hit The Line
scenarios.trigger: If Dance In The Storm and Monarch's Gold press the pace and peg back a tiring Power Fizz in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Power Fizz sustains the front but the effort of leading the full 7f on Good ground catches up in the closing stages as the two prominent hold-up types arrive; Oisin Murphy's timing on Dance In The Storm and Toby Moore's positioning on Monarch's Gold make them the most dangerous pair to capitalise. Dance In The Storm has winning form at 7f on Good ground and returns with a yard firing at 8/45 over 14 days.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If Power Fizz and prominent horses force a faster tempo than expected, opening a late closing lane.
scenarios.body: A contested gallop opens ground for a hold-up horse to pick off rivals in the short straight, though Chester's turning track with its minimal straight is structurally hostile to true closers. Palmar Bay's course form and Harry Vigors's 5lb claim give it the best profile of the genuine hold-up contingent to execute this scenario, while Roman Dragon's "fades in finish" flag works firmly against him despite similar form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos At The Rail
scenarios.trigger: If there is jostling or crowding around the bend that disrupts the front pair and reshuffles the order.
scenarios.body: Chester's tight circuit occasionally produces positional squeeze at pace, particularly with 10 runners; a disrupted race flow could promote the horse who avoids trouble soonest. Khafiz or The Angel King, forced forward from their natural closing style, could inadvertently benefit if the race unravels in front of them — though the structural mismatch between their natural style and the position they are mapped to keeps this a low-probability escape valve.

watchPoints.text: Power Fizz's draw and early break will determine the entire shape of the race — if Cieren Fallon is squeezed or slow to jump, the pace dynamic collapses and the prominent horses inherit control immediately.

Dance In The Storm and Monarch's Gold may press Power Fizz harder than expected on the first bend, with Oisin Murphy unlikely to surrender a prominent pitch cheaply; watch whether Haggas's horse is hassled into going quicker than Fallon would like before halfway.

Palmar Bay (Harry Vigors) and Roman Dragon (David Probert) are both hold-up horses seeking late runs on a track with a minimal straight — any interference or traffic in the final 2f could extinguish either chance before it materialises.

Khafiz, The Angel King, and Korker are all genuine closers racing out of their natural role in today's field shape — if any of them are caught covering extra ground wide through the bend trying to improve, their finishing efforts will be compromised further than their ratings already suggest.

races.name: J20 Classified Claiming Stakes

runners_data.name: Candonomore
runners_data.note: Holds a win at 8f on Firm and figures on similar ground, but Good is within range; true hold-up runner who needs traffic to part late, and the Chester short straight makes that a fine margin — tp headgear has featured consistently, suggesting she needs the visual sharpener to fully commit.|
runners_data.comment: Candonomore brings solid experience over today's trip and conditions, and his win and second in recent starts show he can hit form — drawn in stall 3 carrying 132 lb, the main risk is that his last three runs have been disappointing.

runners_data.name: Alpha Capture
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's six-year-old arrives in career form — a win and two placed efforts in the last three starts at 7f on Good — and Kevin Stott's Chester experience is a genuine asset; naturally prominent and will slot directly behind Blue Prince, making him the primary danger to the leader.|
runners_data.comment: Alpha Capture brings strong recent profile — second two starts back and a winner three starts back, with experience of today's trip and going working in his favour at 130 lb from stall 5; the concern is that unplaced run last time out.

runners_data.name: I Still Have Faith
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams has a modest 14-day strike rate and this horse has not won in recent starts; a natural prominent racer who is crowded out of her ideal berth by Blue Prince and Alpha Capture ahead, meaning she must settle mid-pack and produce a finish that does not entirely suit her — that gap in comfort undermines her here.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, I Still Have Faith nonetheless shapes as a leading danger — he has run over today's trip and going before, and at 128 lb from stall 2, his rating of 84 leaves room to threaten; the risk is that elusive winning form.

runners_data.name: Blue Prince
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride for David Evans on the highest-rated runner in the field; three consecutive third-place finishes at 7-8f precede his Chester win last time and he is the only confirmed pace-maker — one-paced tendencies are a mild concern in the straight, but uncontested control around this track is a significant compensating factor.|
runners_data.comment: Blue Prince arrives on the back of consecutive thirds but was a winner three starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going gives him a solid platform. Drawn in stall four carrying 125 lb, he is the one to beat on rated form.

runners_data.name: Calyxoh
runners_data.note: Patrick Morris has zero winners from 10 runners over the last 14 days, and this four-year-old's recent record shows a win sandwiched between several poor efforts — wears a visor which can sharpen focus; a genuine hold-up horse who cannot get back to his natural position in this field, and the redistribution to midfield is an awkward compromise on a track that doesn't flatter those who switch off early.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts with only a single third to show for it, Calyxoh arrives fresh enough on eight days' rest and has run over today's trip and going — but ranked fifth of six on our figures, he faces a stiff task from stall six carrying 125 lb.

runners_data.name: Midnight Strike
runners_data.note: Candlish's second runner here won over 8f on Good going and has been freshened on 15 days' rest; tp headgear suggests she needs assistance to maintain concentration, and her two-mile stepping-down from 10f in recent runs means stamina for this trip is solid — she is a true hold-up type who needs the pace to have been genuine to strike.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of six on our figures and winless in his last five starts, Midnight Strike won two starts back but has been well beaten in most recent outings; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a 15-day turnaround at least suggests freshness.

races.paceDynamic: Blue Prince is the lone confirmed front runner here and, with no rival likely to seriously contest that position from the gate, he can dictate a controlled, sustainable tempo around Chester's tight circuit over 7½f. Alpha Capture will push forward to claim the best prominent berth directly behind, while I Still Have Faith, though a natural prominent type, is squeezed out of her preferred position by the traffic ahead and must settle a little further back than ideal. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the shape can accommodate in their natural roles — Blue Prince and Alpha Capture are likeliest to secure the lead and second spot, with I Still Have Faith and Calyxoh effectively racing out of their truest positions. A steady, uncontested lead at Chester, where the track's constant turning and short home straight rewards those who conserve energy in transit and kick off a fair pace rather than a searching one, heavily favours horses that can race handily without expending energy fighting for position — Blue Prince dictating and Alpha Capture tracking are ideally placed, and the race shape ultimately tilts toward the lead-to-prominent profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Blue Prince Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Blue Prince rolls forward uncontested and sets a measured, rail-hugging pace through the tight Chester turns.
scenarios.body: Blue Prince, carrying top weight but drawn for the track and ridden by Oisin Murphy who is adept at judging fractions, can conserve enough in front to repel challenges on the short run-in; the Chester circuit's premium on accurate positioning and rail access amplifies the advantage of uncontested lead control.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pull Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Alpha Capture uses Kevin Stott's positional intelligence to sit a length off Blue Prince and pounces when the leader ties up inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Alpha Capture's strong recent form — two wins and multiple places at 7f on good going — makes him the most dangerous prominent challenger if the front-runner fades under pressure late; this shape suits a horse with proven course-distance profile and a jockey who rides Chester regularly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Sweep Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves faster than it looks, tying up the prominent horses and leaving a gap for hold-up finishers to swoop.
scenarios.body: Candonomore won over this trip on Firm going and is the most credible true hold-up runner in the field; Midnight Strike, who won over 8f on good going, could also stay on if the pace has genuinely stretched the field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Unravels, Outsider Lands
scenarios.trigger: If Blue Prince is slow away or pressured early, removing the single pace anchor and creating a messy, contested scramble.
scenarios.body: Without a calm pace setter, energy is wasted early on the tight Chester turns and the form book becomes less reliable; horses with headgear sharpening focus — Candonomore and Midnight Strike both carry tp — could benefit from the resulting tactical chaos.

watchPoints.text: Blue Prince — if he idles in front under Murphy's quiet hands, he could be swamped in the final 100 yards by Alpha Capture lobbing into him off a steady tempo; watch whether Stott sends Alpha Capture sooner than expected.

I Still Have Faith — her natural habit is to push forward and the tactical squeeze into a mid-group role may cause her to race keenly and idle her energy away before the straight; if she breaks alertly, she could outrun her mapped position entirely.

Calyxoh — the visor is there for a reason and his form is wildly inconsistent (9-0-9-7-3 in recent runs); if he gets a clean run from midfield he could be involved in a place, but his redistribution out of his natural hold-up spot makes him volatile rather than dangerous.

Midnight Strike — has dropped significantly in trip from 10f to 7½f and the Candlish yard has a decent recent strike rate at Chester; she is a watch in running for late momentum if the pace has been genuine enough to string the field out.|

races.name: Tom Jones Live At Chester Racecourse Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Farasi Lane
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator who rarely gets involved early; two wins at the sim-going band but all recent form at shorter trips than today's 1m2½f, making the step up in distance the key query here for the Hammond yard.
runners_data.comment: Farasi Lane landed a winner two starts back and has experience over today's trip and going, with our rating of 86 suggesting he holds strong claims here; the main risk is that fifth last time out hints he may need things to fall right.

runners_data.name: Secret Beach
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with an excellent similar-going record of 2W6P from 11 runs, and this 10f Chester trip suits his profile; Moore's 7lb claim is an asset at the weights but the horse's form string shows the last four runs have been modest finishes outside the places.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out and boasting experience over today's trip and conditions, Secret Beach is a lively threat at 142 lb from stall six, with his rating of 81 giving him strong claims; the risk is he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Saligo Bay
runners_data.note: Proven winner at 16f on soft, dropping back considerably to 10f on good today, which is a big question mark; races prominently and the England yard is 2/17 in the 14-day window, so no strong trainer form to compensate for the trip and going doubts.
runners_data.comment: Saligo Bay brings decent recent form — a winner last time out and a second two starts back — and has run over today's distance and going before, but his stall-one draw and a speed rating of 73 that trails his official mark slightly suggest he faces a stiff task against stronger-rated rivals.

runners_data.name: Naples
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner; Hollinshead's 4yo has not won on good going and has been beaten out of sight in recent handicaps, but Costello can control pace here and the unchallenged lead position is a structural advantage regardless of raw ability.
runners_data.comment: Naples has run over today's trip and going and rates as the pick of the field on our figures, which have him top of the ratings; drawn in stall 3 carrying 139 lb, the concern is that he has been out of the frame in two of his last three starts.

runners_data.name: Tiger
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with placings at 10f-12f on soft, stepping back to good ground today where his record is thin; Ian Williams has three runners from 38 in the 14-day window, suggesting steady but not red-hot form, and the 49-day break needs noting.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Tiger nonetheless shaped with promise when second last time out, and he has experience of today's distance and going to call on — 49 days between runs is the one query, but a rating of 84 gives him solid claims from stall 5 carrying 138 lb.

runners_data.name: Echalar
runners_data.note: Williams's second string, also a hold-up type; four runs on good going with three placed finishes suggests the surface is fine, but the recent 17-day turnaround and a form string showing no win in six runs limits confidence despite the capable Probert booking.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked last on our figures, Echalar faces a stiff task from stall eight carrying 137 lb, though he has shown some consistency with a third two starts back and a fourth last time out — small encouragement from an otherwise moderate recent profile.

runners_data.name: Oman
runners_data.note: Carroll's 8yo won at 9f on soft last time and shows a hold-up style by nature — the redistribution to midfield in this map reflects genuine crowding at the rear of the field, so its true closing run may be further compromised by Chester's tight home straight; style-fit concern applies.
runners_data.comment: Oman has been out of the frame in his last two starts, and his recent record of one win in his last six offers little encouragement; however, he has distance and going experience to draw on, and 27 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Moon Beginnings
runners_data.note: Loughnane's 4yo carries a fades-in-finish flag alongside a hold-up tendency, and at a track where getting back is tactically costly, the combination of that flag and the crowded rear makes this a difficult winning profile; the trainer has had no winners from 17 attempts in the 14-day window.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Moon Beginnings does at least bring experience of today's trip and going, and a fourth two starts back hints at some residual ability; however, the eighth last time and fifth before it are a concern, and 134 lb from stall 10 adds no favours.

runners_data.name: Cape Fear
runners_data.note: Balding's 3yo has an outstanding similar-going record of 1W6P from 7 runs and consistently finishes in the frame; races prominently with Oisin Murphy aboard, which is a significant jockey upgrade, and the 3yo weight allowance gives a further edge in a wide-open handicap.
runners_data.comment: Cape Fear has been a model of consistency in recent starts — third last time out, a winner two starts back — and returns after 22 days on familiar distance and going; his 133 lb burden and ranking sixth of ten suggest he'll be competing for a share rather than the spoils.

runners_data.name: Eagle Day
runners_data.note: Evans's 6yo also carries a fades-in-finish warning alongside a hold-up profile; placed once in 15 runs on comparable going, and the redistribution to midfield means this horse is unlikely to find its natural position, making the structural fit for a big run here poor.
runners_data.comment: Eagle Day has managed just one win in his last six starts, with a ninth two runs back hardly inspiring confidence, and ranked ninth of ten on our figures he faces a stiff task; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 12 days since his last outing suggests he arrives fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Naples is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Dougie Costello can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop around Chester's tight track at whatever tempo suits. Secret Beach and Cape Fear will push up to race prominently just behind, with Saligo Bay also likely to track them, creating a small cluster of prominent types that will compress the early order. The redistributed hold-up horses — Oman, Moon Beginnings, and Eagle Day — are true closers by nature but cannot all slot into the deep rear against a field already stacked with prominent runners; at least one or two will find themselves racing closer to midfield than their handler intends. A controlled front-running pace on a galloping track like Chester at 1m2½f historically suits prominent racers that can conserve energy and deliver a sustained challenge in the straight, making the stalking prominent profile the most advantaged shape in this race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Naples Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Naples settles into an uncontested lead and Costello controls the tempo, allowing the prominent duo to chase without burning up.
scenarios.body: Naples rolls along at a measured clip, keeping something in reserve around Chester's bends, and the race plays into the hands of the nearest chasers who get a soft lead to attack late; Cape Fear and Secret Beach, both proven on good ground and comfortable racing close to pace, are ideally positioned to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overwhelm Lead
scenarios.trigger: If Secret Beach or Cape Fear press Naples hard early, lifting the tempo and stringing the field out before the home straight.
scenarios.body: A stronger pace develops as two or three prominent types race close together, burning out Naples inside the final two furlongs and elevating a hard-pressing stalker to the fore; Cape Fear's consistent recent form on good ground and Saligo Bay's proven ability to win from a prominent position both suit a race run with genuine competition from the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough to create gaps in the straight and a midfield horse produces a well-timed run through beaten rivals.
scenarios.body: Tiger or Echalar, both with scope for a strong sustained finish at this trip, would benefit if those ahead have raced too keenly and the rail or a gap presents itself in the home straight; Tiger's course-distance profile at 1m2½f and Echalar's run of placed finishes suggest either could capitalise on a muddled finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely and the genuine hold-up horses — Oman, Moon Beginnings, Eagle Day — secure their natural rear position and get a clear late run.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on the redistributed closers actually finding room on Chester's tight circuit late, which is structurally unlikely given their probable midfield placement; if it does materialise, Oman's one win at 9f on soft suggests good ground may not fully suit, making this the weakest of the four outcomes.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Secret Beach or Cape Fear applies pressure to Naples in the early stages — if either pushes forward aggressively out of the stalls, the controlled tempo that defines the dominant scenario breaks down immediately.

Monitor Oman, Moon Beginnings, and Eagle Day in the betting: if any drifts significantly, it may reflect market awareness that Chester's tight circuit and a crowded midfield strips them of their best-case closing shape.

Saligo Bay's trip drop from 16f to 10f is sharp — if Tom Eaves sends him forward to take up a prominent position, watch whether he has the speed to sustain it at this shorter distance on good ground rather than his favoured soft.

Cape Fear's 3yo allowance and Oisin Murphy's booking make him a horse to watch in the market; if he shortens noticeably pre-race, it would confirm market confidence in the prominent-racer profile that this race shape most favours.
Naples's in-running price will be the key race-reading signal — if he is allowed to bowl along unopposed at a low price in-running, the SCENARIO_A shape is crystallising in real time.
